scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:67 - `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed and fails on Linux.. GNU sed doesn't take a separate argument after `-i`. On Linux, `''` is read as the sed script and the `s|...|` expression is read as a filename, so the command errors out and `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated. The script still prints the ✅ success message afterwards. Use a portable form, for example `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`. Also, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved from the caller's working directory, not from the script's location.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022 - Leftover SelectedCalendar write adds a DB update on every cache refresh, likely a no-op.. The cache status the UI shows comes from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`). Nothing in this PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so this looks left over from an earlier approach. Every webhook-driven availability refresh now runs an extra `updateMany` over all of the credential's selected calendars. Because it is awaited with no error handling, a failure here also fails the refresh after the cache was already written. On top of that, `updateMany` with empty `data: {}` most likely does not bump `@updatedAt` in Prisma, so the write probably does nothing useful. Remove this call. The related `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` additions in `user.ts` and `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` are probably leftovers too.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24 - Access-denied case throws a plain Error, which the client sees as a 500.. A plain `Error` reaches the client as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a missing or not-owned credential looks like a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`) instead.

packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 - Existing cache rows are backfilled with the migration time, so stale caches look freshly updated.. Every existing `CalendarCache` row gets `updatedAt` set to the moment this migration runs. The new cache status UI reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from this column, so right after deploy it shows every existing cache as just updated, even ones that are old or about to expire. To avoid this, backfill from an existing column where possible (for example, derive it from `expiresAt`). Otherwise, accept that the status is inaccurate until each cache is next written.
